title: Thanthai Periyar and the University Students: Science, Reason, and Humanist Ethics
summary: Addressing inquisitive university students, Thanthai Periyar demonstrated how scientific inquiry and humanist empathy must replace blind adherence to ancient scriptures.
keywords: Historical Dialogue 149: ஐசன்ஹவரும் அணிலின் தட்டலும்: “இது ஒரு பைத்தியக்கார விடுதி!”
full_text:
In the late 1950s, Thanthai Periyar was invited to speak before a packed assembly of college and university students in Tiruchirappalli.

During the interactive session, a physics student stood up to challenge him:
"Ayya, our ancient epics and mythological traditions describe countless miracles and supernatural occurrences. Can we legitimately dismiss all of them as falsehoods? Might they not conceal esoteric scientific truths?"

Periyar smiled warmly, stroked his flowing white beard, and responded with brilliant pedagogical clarity:
"My young friend, that is an excellent question. But there is a fundamental touchstone by which one distinguishes genuine science from dogma.

Authentic science is the fruit of verifiable human inquiry and reproducible effort. When Thomas Edison invented the electric incandescent bulb, he created a technology that works for everyone. When a switch is turned on, the lamp illuminates the room equally for the believer, the agnostic, the scholar, and the manual laborer. Science does not inspect a person’s caste, creed, or ritual purity!
Conversely, supernatural claims in ancient texts often demand unconditional surrender to authority and justify social inequalities. Whatever divides humanity and demands blind belief is superstition. Whatever unites human beings, relieves suffering, and invites rigorous questioning is true science! Never accept a statement merely because it was written on ancient palm leaves—test everything with your own critical intellect!"

The hall reverberated with energetic applause as the students absorbed the liberating clarity of the scientific method applied to social ethics.
